potaliputta.notes: MN 136 places the Buddha at the Bamboo Grove and Samiddhi in a wilderness hut. It is at the hut that the wanderer approaches Samiddhi.

potaliya.notes: MN 54 calls Potaliya a gahapati and recounts his objection to that title. AN 4.100 calls its speaker a paribbājaka and discusses praise and criticism. DPD cites both under the householder. DPPN suggests they may be the same man, but neither discourse establishes that. The MN 53 page hit belongs to MN 54.

pubbajira.notes: MN 144 names the village. The citation lands in MN 143. The parallel at SN 35.87:13.5 reads pubbavijjanaṁ, a separate DPD headword. Both discourses describe families there who were close to Channa. DPPN's claim that the villagers were blamed for his death misstates the exchange about Channa's own blamelessness.

pubbavideha.notes: AN 3.80:4.2 and AN 10.29:2.2 both list pubbavidehānaṁ among the continents of a world system. Sujato translates the name as lands east of Videha, so the English name filter misses it. MN 50:30.3 and Thag 20.1:63.3 use the same form for the inhabitants.

pukkusa.notes: DN 16 names the Mallian disciple of Āḷāra Kālāma. Pukkusa 04 describes a caste. MN 93 and AN 4.85 use pukkusakula in lists of families, and AN 4.84 is a neighboring page hit.

pukkusāti.notes: Both senses refer to stages of the life described in this entry. MN 140:3.1 says the kulaputta had already gone forth. He dies before formal ordination and is declared a non-returner. SN 1.50 and SN 2.24 name Pukkusāti among the seven freed in Aviha. MN 139 and SN 1.49 are adjacent citation hits.

punabbasu.notes: His mother addresses the young yakkha in SN 10.7. SN 10.8 is Sudatta's discourse. The occurrence at SN 10.12:14.3 is in the chapter's closing list of discourses.

purāṇa.notes: MN 89 and SN 55.6 call the pair isidattapurāṇā thapatayo, which has its own dictionary line. Migasālā names her father Purāṇa in AN 6.44 and AN 10.75. The cited list at AN 6.120–139:1.12 spells the name Pūraṇa, immediately before Isidatta. AN 6.119 and AN 6.140 are neighboring page hits.

puṇḍarīka.notes: SN 6.10:6.10–11 spells the White Lotus hell puṇḍarika with a short i. AN 10.89:15.12–13 and Snp 3.10:8.10–11 use long ī. All three compare its duration with twenty lifetimes in the preceding hell. The packet misses the translated name, and the tap on puṇḍarīko lacks the hell sense even in the long-ī texts.

puṇṇa.notes: Thag 1.4 names Mantāṇiputta in its attribution. Thag 1.70 credits the second Puṇṇa with the exact verse given to the Sunāparanta elder by DPD and DPPN. The two Therīgāthā hits name nuns. Review Puṇṇa 04 before including it. At MN 93:18.71 Ṭhānissaro reads puṇṇo dabbigāho as a ladle-holder named Puṇṇa, as DPPN does. Sujato reads a ritual spoonful and gives the Vedic parallels in his note. This is the only proposed passage for the servant. MN 94 is an adjacent hit. In MN 57:2.1 acelo qualifies Seniya, while Puṇṇa is called the Koliyan cow votary. MN 56 and the AN groups flanking AN 1.196 are also page overlaps. Claude: Puṇṇa 04 doesn't ship: Sujato's English, which the app shows, reads MN 93's puṇṇo dabbigāho as a ritual spoonful, not a person.

puṇṇaka.notes: DN 32 lists Puṇṇaka among the spirits to whom an appeal can be made. Snp 5.1 and 5.18 list him among the brahmin students, and Snp 5.4 records his questions.

puṇṇikā.notes: MN 99:11.2 identifies Pokkharasāti's maid. The DPD sense fits the water-carrier addressed as Puṇṇikā at Thig 12.1:3.2, whose verse is signed Puṇṇā Therī. Neither passage connects her to Pokkharasāti. Showing the sole candidate as the nun's biography would conflate the two.

puṇṇiya.notes: The monk asks what inspires the Buddha to teach in AN 8.82 and AN 10.83. AN 8.81 is a neighboring citation. AN 10.90:8.1 mentions Puṇṇiya in the chapter summary.

pācīnavaṁsa.notes: SN 15.20:2.3 gives this earlier name of Mount Vepulla. The citations to SN 15.18 and SN 15.19 share its page.

pācīnavaṁsadāya.notes: AN 8.30 locates the park in Ceti country. MN 128:8.1 names it as the residence of Anuruddha, Nandiya, and Kimbila. The same three stay at Gosiṅga in MN 31. Check DPPN's placement of Meghiya here. AN 9.3 and Ud 4.1 put his mango grove by the Kimikālā near Jantugāma. AN 8.8, AN 8.29, and MN 30 also lack this park.

pāricchattaka.notes: AN 7.69:1.1 identifies the tree by name and by the gods who celebrate its growth. Sujato calls it the Shady Orchid Tree, so the packet misses it. AN 7.68 is an adjacent page hit. SN 48.68 uses the spelling pārichattako, which has a separate DPD line.

pāvā.notes: MN 104:2.1 places the death of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta at Pāvā. MN 103 is an adjacent page hit.

pāyāsi.notes: DN 23:32.3 already identifies Uttara as the organizer of Pāyāsi's offering when he makes his criticism. DPPN describes him as a disappointed recipient appointed afterward.

pāṭaligāma.notes: DN 16 and Ud 8.6 connect Pāṭali Village with the future Pāṭaliputta. References to the later city include AN 5.50, MN 52, MN 94, and SN 45.18. AN 5.49, MN 51, MN 95, and SN 45.15–17 are page overlaps. The AN 11 parallel is 11.16, beyond both cited numbers. In Ud 8.6 the ministers Sunīdha and Vassakāra offer the meal that DPPN attributes to the villagers.

ragā.notes: SN 4.25 names Māra's three daughters, as does the verse at Snp 4.9:1.1. SN 4.24 is an adjacent page hit.

rakkhita.notes: MN 116 lists a privately awakened Buddha. The candidate describes the elder credited with Thag 1.79.

rakkhitavanasaṇḍa.notes: Ud 4.5 gives the forest, the sal tree, and the elephant. Its own account says the Buddha sought solitude because of the crowds at Kosambī.

rammaka.notes: MN 26 names Rammaka as the brahmin whose hermitage the monks visit. MN 25 is an adjacent page hit.
